figures.finding: Benin has no rule of its own for child performers: the Children's Code makes a young worker a child of at least fourteen who has finished primary school (the Labour Code's floor of fourteen, layer 3), forbids a child's working more than four hours a day without rest and all night work, and bars the worst forms of child labour (pornographic shows among them) and any work harmful to health, schooling or development; no permit, schooling or chaperone rule for performing exists, and nothing distinguishes writing or directing.

figures.finding: Benin is a party to the OHADA Treaty (in force there from 1995-09-18), so its company law is OHADA's: a minor who is not emancipated may not be a trader or do commercial acts (Uniform Act on general commercial law, art. 7), and minors may be partners only in a company where they are not liable for its debts beyond their contribution (Uniform Act on commercial companies, art. 8), so a young producer's vehicle can be an SARL or SA in which the minor holds shares, never a general partnership; the Acts set no age of their own for a manager, and a person under a legal incapacity may not be a partner (art. 7), so the national age of majority governs. In Benin a minor may be emancipated from sixteen (Persons and Family Code art. 535) and is then capable as an adult (art. 537), so may trade.

figures.finding: Benin's age of majority is eighteen: the Persons and Family Code makes a minor anyone not yet eighteen (art. 459), and the Children's Code gives 'mineur' the same sense; an unmarried minor of sixteen may be emancipated by the court on the parents' request, and marriage emancipates (arts. 534, 535), the emancipated minor being capable as an adult of every act of civil life (art. 537).

value.basis: Code des personnes et de la famille arts. 459, 534-537; Code de l'enfant art. 2

figures.finding: In Benin a minor's work in any artistic activity is forbidden unless the minor's legal guardian or the Labour Inspectorate authorises it (Statut de l'artiste, art. 29), and the statute's 'artist' is any creator or performer of works of the mind in the arts and letters, so the rule reaches a young writer or director as well as a performer; what the child earns by work is outside the parents' legal enjoyment of the child's property (Persons and Family Code art. 455), though it is managed under the legal administration or guardianship until majority (art. 459). No share of the earnings must be set aside.

value.binding: authorisation of the legal guardian or the Labour Inspectorate
